newsitem.title: USA: Some U.S. spot resid prices erode despite crude.
newsitem.headline: Some U.S. spot resid prices erode despite crude.

text.p: Some U.S. spot residual fuel prices continued to erode Friday despite firmer crude, still pressured by soft bunkers, mild East Coast weather and prospects for better avails, particularly of high sulphurs.
"There's no demand from utilities, and high sulphur may be a little heavy," said one cash trader, adding one factor that could stem the slide would be another rally in crude.

At the U.S. Gulf, lack of demand from Florida continued to pressure low sulphur grades, with one percent off 25-50 cents to $19.25-50. USG three percent, hit by softer bunkers, fell 50 cents to about $18.50, traders said.
In New York Harbor, high sulphurs were steady to down slightly, with three percent, also undermined by softer bunkers in the region, now talked around $19.50.

NYH physical one percent held relatively steady at about $21.25 a barrel, while November paper gained more than 25 cents with crude to about the $21 mark. December paper was talked just slightly over November levels, also up on the day.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.

Mild weather pressured New York City gate weekend gas prices down another 10 cents Friday to the low-$2.70s/mmBtu versus NYH one percent resid at a $3.37/mmBtu equivalent. November New York gas firmed about 10 cents to about the $3.20 level compared to a resid paper equivalent of about $3.33.
